chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), regarding:

A man who frees his male slave or female slave manumission from behind (upon his death), then he needs the value of the slave, should he sell him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, unless he stipulates upon the one to whom he sells him that he frees him upon his death.

key_terms.عَن دُبُرٍ: Manumission deferred until the master's death

ai.seo_question: Can a master sell a slave whose manumission is deferred until his death if he needs money?
ai.summary: This ruling from *al-Istibsar* clarifies that the deferred manumission of a *mudabbarr* is not voided by sale, provided the condition of eventual freedom is preserved for the buyer. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on maintaining the integrity of the master's emancipation pledge even when the asset is liquidated, ensuring the slave's path to freedom remains secure.
